map.summary: This subsystem implements dense-query retrieval for a multi-tenant hybrid RAG backend: an injected embedding provider turns a normalized query into a vector used in a k-NN search against an OpenSearch read alias, and hits are renormalized into the shared RetrievalResult contract reused by lexical retrieval. Configuration derives from Settings, diagnostics are separated into a trace, and the only local entry point is a debug CLI, with orchestration living elsewhere.
unknowns: How dense retrieval is composed with lexical, hybrid, or reranked retrieval is not shown by any supplied finding.
No supplied finding exposes a public search API or caller; the module docstring states orchestration for dense retrieval lives elsewhere.
Behavior of supporting modules (models/retrieval.py, retrieval_filters.py, opensearch_index.py, providers/*) beyond dense_retrieval imports is not described.
Tests are listed but their assertions and coverage of the dense path are not detailed.

diagrams.title: Architecture
diagrams.description: Settings feed a dense retrieval config; the retriever injects an embedding provider and queries OpenSearch through a read alias, emitting shared RetrievalResults while reusing lexical parsing for one result contract.

diagrams.title: Request Lifecycle
diagrams.description: A query is normalized, validated, embedded, and issued as a k-NN search; empty queries short-circuit before any external call, and stage timings plus diagnostics are recorded in the trace.

diagrams.title: Debug CLI Entry
diagrams.description: The only local entry point is a debug CLI that parses query, tenant, and optional collection/limit, opens the configured embedding provider, and builds the retriever from settings.

F0001.statement: OpenSearchDenseRetriever is the dense retrieval entry point: search() normalizes the query, builds RetrievalFilters, embeds the query, issues a k-NN search against the read alias, and returns a DenseRetrievalResponse.

F0002.statement: DenseRetrievalConfig pairs an embedding model/dimensions with an index schema version and candidate limit, and from_settings derives these from Settings fields (cohere_embed_model, cohere_embed_dimensions, opensearch_index_schema_version, opensearch_dense_candidate_limit).

F0003.statement: OpenSearchDenseRetriever.from_settings constructs the retriever from Settings (opensearch_url, opensearch_read_alias) plus a caller-supplied EmbeddingProvider, making the provider an injected dependency rather than created internally.

F0004.statement: Query text is normalized by normalize_dense_query (whitespace collapse), and an empty normalized query short-circuits to an empty DenseRetrievalResponse with zeroed timings and candidate counts, skipping both embedding and OpenSearch calls.

F0005.statement: The embedding provider is called via embed(EmbeddingRequest((normalized_query,), EmbeddingPurpose.QUERY)); the returned EmbeddingResult is validated in _query_vector for purpose, vector count, model match, dimension match, and finite numeric values, raising RetrievalError with non-retryable codes otherwise.

F0006.statement: The search body uses an OpenSearch knn query on field 'embedding' with k and a bool filter built from RetrievalFilters.clauses(), scoping results to tenant and optional collection/source_type/author/date filters.

F0007.statement: Dense hits are converted to shared RetrievalResult objects by reusing OpenSearchBM25Retriever._result_from_hit and _candidate_count, so dense and lexical retrieval share one normalized result contract.

F0008.statement: The _source projection requested from OpenSearch fields includes chunk_id, tenant_id, collection_id, document_id, document_content_id, content_text, source_spans, generation_id, pipeline_version, and source_metadata.

F0009.statement: _request opens an httpx.AsyncClient per call with a 10-second timeout and optional injected transport; HTTP transport errors map to RetrievalError('opensearch_unavailable', retryable=True), and error responses map to the same code with retryable true for status >=500 or 408/429, false otherwise.

F0010.statement: Malformed OpenSearch bodies (non-dict payload, non-dict hits, non-list hits.hits) raise RetrievalError('opensearch_invalid_response', retryable=False).

F0011.statement: DenseRetrievalResponse separates public evidence (tuple of RetrievalResult) from non-public diagnostics in DenseRetrievalTrace, which records normalized query, model/dimensions, adapter, schema version, alias, candidate limit/count, per-stage elapsed milliseconds, tenant_id, collection_id, and filter trace values.

F0012.statement: Embedding and OpenSearch stages are timed separately using time.perf_counter (embedding_elapsed_ms, opensearch_elapsed_ms) and only embedding timing is recorded for the empty-query short-circuit (as zero).

F0013.statement: Effective candidate limit is min(limit, config.candidate_limit) when a positive limit is supplied, otherwise the configured default; non-positive or boolean limits raise ValueError.

F0014.statement: The only local entry point is a CLI (main) that parses query, required --tenant UUID, optional --collection UUID and --limit, then runs asyncio.run(_debug_query(...)); the module docstring states no public search API is exposed yet, indicating orchestration for dense retrieval lives elsewhere.

F0015.statement: _debug_query opens configured_cohere_embeddings as an async context manager to obtain the provider, builds the retriever via from_settings, and calls search with debug=True.

F0016.statement: DenseRetrievalConfig.__post_init__ calls physical_index_name(self.index_schema_version, "dense-query") to validate the schema-version contract, with an inline comment stating dense retrieval trusts the configured model/index pairing and intentionally does not issue a mapping request per query.
